title: Lester Young's tiny sound and the great tenor players
summary: Freeman says he and Lester shared the Louis beat; Lester swung everything with a small sound, and Freeman praises Ben Webster, Getz and Eddie Miller.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Yes, well, that's very true because many people have said that we play a little alike. I am not too sure about that, but I only know that we were influenced by the same people. You can hear -- in fact, I have written about this in the first book called You Don't Look Like A Musician -- I was very much influenced by Louis and you can hear that Louis beat in Lester.

Maybe Lester wouldn't have thought of it as being a Louis beat, but you see, the difference between Lester Young's playing and all the other tenor players was that Lester swung everything he played. He never played a phrase to show off technique. He had the facility, he was a brilliant musician, but he played -- he was probably the most honest tenor player I have ever heard, because he just played what he felt and he had that -- now Hawkins had the great big sound that all

tenor players at that time were trying to copy. Lester came in with that little tiny sound and took over the whole world and when I heard it -- now, again, I had started to play eight years before this -- when I heard that, it reminded me of something I had heard many, many years ago in Chicago, that wonderful beat and the conservation of notes, the wonderful taste, and in my view, and it's just my opinion, having been there, Lester Young was the most interesting tenor player.
Now, again, I don't mean to say that I didn't admire Hawkins, which I did, and I thought really that Ben Webster was the best ballad tenor player I had ever heard of.

Now, there are many tenor players I admire. I admire Stan Getz, there are so many different players that I have tremendous regard for. Eddie Miller who played in beautiful taste, lovely sound and all that.
